cells.tense: You are here at the bench now, with the pen already moving.
cells.ask: Before you walk into one room today, name out loud the one move you'll make to steady it. Then make it while saying what you're doing.
cells.core:
A table turns toward its people when you sit at it. Talk finds its pace, someone braced lets go, and nothing visibly steered it. That isn't a mood you arrived with. It's a craft built by repetition and kept lit by attention — you know whose pause means what, which silence wants leaving alone, when one word does it. You fit the room to the people in it.

The next move is to let the working show. Say what you're doing while you do it, once, for one person, so the craft stops reading as luck. What follows is that the room gets steadied in the open, with your hand visible on it.
cells.sheetLine: What settles a table when you sit at it is a craft you built.

cells.place: the small room where a thing is practised alone, by repetition, until it becomes skill

cells.tense: You are leaning into next week's room, trying to hear how it ought to feel.
cells.ask: Choose one gathering. Walk in without arranging it first, and stay through the middle before you check how it's going.
cells.core:
The version that works is quick and light: you enter, read the room in a breath, put one steadying word where it's needed, and let the rest belong to the people in it. You notice shoulders come down and voices find their level, and you don't have to hold any of it after. That's the size of the craft when it's turning well.

Your reading has outrun the room itself. You arrange the air before anyone has arrived, warm a gathering still days off, smooth a conversation that hasn't happened. The speed the craft needs is smaller than the speed it's running at, and what you're tending hasn't asked you yet.

cells.tense: You are stopped at a door you already went through, and not stepping back in.
cells.ask: Tell one person one true thing about how you are today. Short, about you, not about them, no context needed.
cells.core:
The version that works is easy from where you stand: a room's temperature is legible, a phrase adjusts it, and you can tend the middle without getting swallowed. You catch whose shoulders drop, whose voice goes quiet, and you put one small thing in the right place. The craft is still there and it still reads true.

What's missing is the next small move — the steadying word, the let-it-out adjustment. You hold the doorway instead of the exchange. The reading runs, and the stepping in has stopped, so the room gets watched rather than entered.
cells.sheetLine: You read the room fine. You've stopped stepping into it.

cells.tense: You are tending the room you're in and calling it just being decent.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, to one person: "I did that on purpose." Say it about something small you did this week — a pause, a look, a settling.
cells.core:
When this sits right, someone who settles a table knows they settled it. They spot the seam they closed, the minute they let breathe, and can say so afterward. The doing and the saying sit in the same person, and the room gets tended in the open, with the craft going under its own name.

Your doing has run ahead of your saying. You read the temperature, adjust it, keep feeling moving, then file it under being polite or just how people are. The move happened, and it went out into the room unsigned.
cells.sheetLine: You did that on purpose and you keep calling it nothing.
